name: Dynamic SQL built by string concatenation
attack_scenario: p_name is set to `x'' OR ''1''=''1' (or `'; DROP TABLE users; --`); the concatenated statement becomes attacker-controlled SQL that deletes or dumps arbitrary rows.
negative_test_hint: set p_name to "'; DROP TABLE users; --" and assert the users table survives because the value is bound via USING, not concatenated into the statement

exemplar.noncompliant: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'DELETE FROM users WHERE name = ''' || p_name || '''';
exemplar.compliant: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'DELETE FROM users WHERE name = :1' USING p_name;
exemplar.explanation: CWE-89: concatenating variables into an EXECUTE IMMEDIATE / EXEC() / sp_executesql string (with || or +) splices caller input into the query text, so any quote-breaking value alters the statement. OWASP requires parameterized/bind execution (USING binds, sp_executesql @params) instead of concatenation.
